chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.text: This policy governs customer due diligence, sanctions screening, and the compliance assessment of new product applications. It applies to compliance analysts, onboarding staff, and any agent producing findings on their behalf. Transaction monitoring for fraud is governed separately under the Fraud Policy, though the two functions share findings.

chunks.heading: 2. Know your customer requirements
chunks.text: Every customer must have a current identity record on file before any product is opened. The record comprises identity document type, document number, expiry date, verified residential address, politically exposed person status, and a risk rating.

chunks.heading: 2. Know your customer requirements
chunks.text: An identity document past its expiry date invalidates the record. The customer is treated as not verified until a replacement is provided, regardless of how long they have banked with the institution.

chunks.heading: 2. Know your customer requirements
chunks.text: An unverified address is a finding in its own right. Address verification is the control that prevents statement redirection, which is a common precursor to account takeover.

chunks.heading: 3. Absence of a record is not a finding
chunks.text: An applicant with no customer relationship will have no KYC record. This is expected and must not be reported as a deficiency. New applicants are onboarded through the standard verification process.

chunks.heading: 3. Absence of a record is not a finding
chunks.text: The distinction matters: a missing record on a new applicant is routine, while a missing or lapsed record on an existing customer is a control failure requiring remediation.

chunks.heading: 4. Risk ratings
chunks.text: Low rated customers are reviewed every three years. Medium rated customers are reviewed every two years. High rated customers are reviewed annually, and any product application from a High rated customer requires supervisor approval.

chunks.heading: 4. Risk ratings
chunks.text: A rating is not a judgement about the customer's character and must not be communicated to them as such. It determines review frequency and approval routing, nothing more.

chunks.heading: 4. Risk ratings
chunks.text: A review date more than one cycle overdue is a control failure and must be reported even where every other element of the record is current.

chunks.heading: 5. Politically exposed persons
chunks.text: A politically exposed person holds or has held a prominent public function, or is an immediate family member or close associate of someone who does.

chunks.heading: 5. Politically exposed persons
chunks.text: PEP status is not a reason to decline. It requires enhanced due diligence: senior management approval, establishment of source of wealth, and annual review irrespective of the customer's risk rating.

chunks.heading: 5. Politically exposed persons
chunks.text: PEP status must be re-checked at every review, because the customer's circumstances may have changed since onboarding.

chunks.heading: 6. Sanctions screening
chunks.text: Every applicant name is screened against the consolidated sanctions list before any product is opened, and every existing customer is rescreened whenever the list is updated.

chunks.heading: 6. Sanctions screening
chunks.text: Screening is fuzzy by design. Sanctioned parties deliberately vary spelling, transliteration, and word order, so exact matching alone would miss most genuine hits. The consequence is a high volume of false positives, and this is expected rather than a defect.

chunks.heading: 6. Sanctions screening
chunks.text: A similarity score is a measure of textual resemblance. It is not a probability that the customer is sanctioned. A score of one point zero means the strings are identical, which most commonly indicates two unrelated people sharing a common name.

chunks.heading: 7. Handling a screening match
chunks.text: An analyst must never record a customer as sanctioned on the strength of a name match. The match is a trigger for verification, not a conclusion.

chunks.heading: 7. Handling a screening match
chunks.text: Verification requires comparison of secondary identifiers: date of birth, nationality, place of birth, and known aliases held on the sanctions record. Where those identifiers are absent from the sanctions entry, the match is escalated to the Sanctions team rather than resolved locally.

chunks.heading: 7. Handling a screening match
chunks.text: Where a match is confirmed, the account is frozen immediately, no funds are released, and the matter is reported to the relevant authority within the statutory period. The customer must not be told why.

chunks.heading: 7. Handling a screening match
chunks.text: Where a match is discounted, the reasoning and the identifiers compared are recorded, and the name is added to the local whitelist so the same false positive is not re-investigated at every screening.

chunks.heading: 8. Suspicious activity reporting
chunks.text: Cash transactions at or above ten thousand dollars require a currency transaction report.

chunks.heading: 8. Suspicious activity reporting
chunks.text: A pattern of transactions immediately below that threshold is treated as possible structuring and reported regardless of the individual amounts.

chunks.heading: 8. Suspicious activity reporting
chunks.text: Compliance staff must never disclose that a report has been filed or contemplated. Tipping off is a criminal offence and applies to any communication with the customer, including hints, delays explained by reference to the report, or advice to withdraw an application.

chunks.heading: 9. Account changes
chunks.text: Any change to address, telephone number, or email requires two factor verification.

chunks.heading: 9. Account changes
chunks.text: Where the identity document on file has expired, no account change may be processed until it is refreshed. This is absolute and there is no discretion.

chunks.heading: 9. Account changes
chunks.text: Changes of contact details for High rated customers require supervisor approval, because contact takeover is a common precursor to account fraud.

chunks.heading: 10. Escalation
chunks.text: Findings are escalated to a compliance manager where a sanctions match cannot be discounted locally, where a customer is identified as a PEP after onboarding, where a review is more than one cycle overdue, or where the same finding recurs on the same customer within twelve months.

chunks.heading: 10. Escalation
chunks.text: Escalations are raised the same working day. A finding held overnight without escalation is a control failure.

chunks.heading: 11. Record keeping
chunks.text: Due diligence records, screening results including discounted matches, and the reasoning for every decision are retained for six years after the relationship ends.

chunks.heading: 11. Record keeping
chunks.text: Quality review samples ten percent of onboarding files monthly. A discounted screening match without recorded identifier comparison, or a processed account change against an expired document, is recorded as a control failure and reported to the audit committee.

chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.text: This policy governs how the bank detects, investigates, and resolves suspected fraud on credit and debit card products. It applies to all analysts in Financial Crime Operations, to automated monitoring systems, and to any agent acting on their behalf. It does not cover first-party fraud on lending products, which is dealt with under the Lending Policy, nor internal staff fraud, which is handled by Group Security.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: A transaction is scored against the cardholder's own history rather than against fixed limits alone. A transaction is flagged for review where any of the following hold.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: The transaction value exceeds five times the cardholder's rolling ninety day average transaction value. This ratio test is the primary detection signal and takes precedence over absolute value tests, because a two thousand dollar transaction is unremarkable for one customer and highly abnormal for another.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: The transaction is booked between 22:00 and 05:59 in the cardholder's registered time zone. Overnight activity is not itself evidence of fraud, but it correlates strongly with account takeover and raises the score.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: The merchant city is one the cardholder has not transacted in during the previous twelve months. Distance is not used, because a customer who travels regularly should not be penalised for it; novelty of location is the signal, not remoteness.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: Four or more transactions are booked on the same card within a single calendar day.

chunks.heading: 2. Detection thresholds
chunks.text: Scores are cumulative. A transaction meeting three or more criteria is treated as high priority and must be reviewed within four hours of flagging.

chunks.heading: 3. Structuring and the reporting threshold
chunks.text: Cash transactions of ten thousand dollars or more require a currency transaction report. Analysts must be alert to structuring, which is the deliberate splitting of a larger sum into amounts that individually fall below the threshold.

chunks.heading: 3. Structuring and the reporting threshold
chunks.text: A single transaction between nine thousand and ten thousand dollars is not, on its own, evidence of structuring. A pattern of such transactions, or a single such transaction combined with other detection signals, must be escalated to the Anti Money Laundering team regardless of whether the individual amounts breach the threshold.

chunks.heading: 3. Structuring and the reporting threshold
chunks.text: Analysts must never inform a customer that a suspicious activity report has been considered or filed. This is tipping off and is a criminal offence under money laundering regulations. Where a customer asks directly, the analyst states only that the matter is under review.

chunks.heading: 4. Investigation procedure
chunks.text: On receiving a flagged transaction, the analyst retrieves the full transaction record and the cardholder's transaction history for at least ninety days. A judgement made on a single transaction without reference to the customer's baseline is not a valid investigation and will fail quality review.

chunks.heading: 4. Investigation procedure
chunks.text: The analyst then establishes whether the pattern is explicable. Common benign explanations include seasonal purchasing, a recorded change of address, a known travel notification on file, and legitimate high value purchases at a new merchant. The absence of transaction history is itself a finding and must be reported as such rather than treated as an absence of risk.

chunks.heading: 4. Investigation procedure
chunks.text: Where the analyst concludes the activity is suspicious, a case is raised. Where the analyst concludes it is explicable, the reasoning is recorded and the flag is cleared. Flags must never be cleared without a recorded reason.

chunks.heading: 5. Raising a fraud case
chunks.text: Cases are raised in the incident management system with a short description naming the transaction identifier, and a description setting out the specific findings. Cases are raised at urgency two by default. Urgency one is reserved for cases where funds may still be recoverable, typically within the first six hours of an unauthorised transaction.

chunks.heading: 5. Raising a fraud case
chunks.text: An agent must obtain explicit confirmation from a human analyst before raising a case. Automated case creation without human sign off is prohibited. This restriction exists because a fraud case attaches to the customer record and affects their ability to transact, and a false positive carries real cost to the customer.

chunks.heading: 6. Customer liability
chunks.text: Where a customer reports a lost or stolen card, liability for unauthorised use before the report is capped at fifty dollars. There is no liability for use after the report.

chunks.heading: 6. Customer liability
chunks.text: Where the bank's own monitoring identifies the fraud before the customer reports it, the customer bears no liability at all.

chunks.heading: 6. Customer liability
chunks.text: Where the investigation concludes the customer authorised the transaction and later disputed it, no liability limit applies and the matter is referred to the disputes team under the Support Policy.

chunks.heading: 7. Card blocking
chunks.text: A flagged transaction results in a soft block. The customer may lift a soft block by confirming identity through two factors.

chunks.heading: 7. Card blocking
chunks.text: An open fraud case prevents an agent from lifting a block. Only the fraud team may authorise removal while a case is open.

chunks.heading: 7. Card blocking
chunks.text: Confirmed fraud results in a hard block. A hard block cannot be lifted under any circumstances and the card must be reissued.

chunks.heading: 8. Cross border transactions
chunks.text: Transactions in jurisdictions subject to enhanced monitoring receive an additional score increment. Jurisdiction alone is never sufficient grounds to decline or to raise a case, and analysts must not treat a country of origin as evidence of wrongdoing. The signal is used only in combination with others.

chunks.heading: 8. Cross border transactions
chunks.text: Recovery of funds sent cross border is materially harder and often impossible once settled. Where a cross border transaction is flagged and still pending, the analyst prioritises it above domestic cases of equivalent score.

chunks.heading: 9. Irreversible payment channels
chunks.text: Cryptocurrency exchanges, money remitters, and prepaid card top ups are treated as irreversible channels. Once funds settle in these channels they cannot be recalled.

chunks.heading: 9. Irreversible payment channels
chunks.text: A flagged transaction to an irreversible channel is escalated one urgency level. Where the transaction is still pending, the analyst may request an immediate hold without waiting for the standard review window.

chunks.heading: 10. Record keeping and review
chunks.text: All investigation reasoning is retained for six years. Cleared flags are retained alongside raised cases, because a pattern of repeatedly cleared flags on one account is itself a supervisory concern.

chunks.heading: 10. Record keeping and review
chunks.text: Quality review samples five percent of closed cases each month. A case closed without reference to customer history, or a case raised without recorded findings, is recorded as a control failure.

chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.text: This policy governs the assessment of consumer loan applications, the affordability tests applied, and the circumstances in which an application must be referred rather than decided. It applies to all credit analysts and to any agent producing a recommendation on their behalf. Commercial lending and mortgage lending are out of scope and are governed separately.

chunks.heading: 2. Recommendations, not decisions
chunks.text: An analyst or agent produces a recommendation of approve, decline, or refer. A recommendation is not a decision. Only an authorised credit officer may record a decision against an application, and no system may present a recommendation to a customer as though it were an outcome.

chunks.heading: 2. Recommendations, not decisions
chunks.text: Every recommendation must state the reasoning and the specific figures relied on. A recommendation that cites a conclusion without the underlying ratios will fail quality review.

chunks.heading: 3. Credit score bands
chunks.text: Credit scores are assessed on a three hundred to nine hundred scale.

chunks.heading: 3. Credit score bands
chunks.text: Scores of seven hundred and fifty and above are treated as strong. Applications in this band may be recommended for approval where affordability tests also pass.

chunks.heading: 3. Credit score bands
chunks.text: Scores between six hundred and fifty and seven hundred and forty nine are acceptable. Approval is available but the affordability tests are applied strictly, with no discretion on marginal cases.

chunks.heading: 3. Credit score bands
chunks.text: Scores between five hundred and fifty and six hundred and forty nine are weak. These applications are referred for manual underwriting regardless of affordability, because the score indicates prior difficulty that the ratios alone will not reveal.

chunks.heading: 3. Credit score bands
chunks.text: Scores below five hundred and fifty are treated as adverse. The recommendation is decline unless there are documented exceptional circumstances, which must be recorded in full.

chunks.heading: 4. Affordability tests
chunks.text: Three ratios are calculated for every application. Analysts judge the ratios; they do not recalculate them, because inconsistent arithmetic between analysts is a recurring source of error.

chunks.heading: 4. Affordability tests
chunks.text: Loan to income is the total advance divided by gross annual income. A ratio at or below two point zero is within appetite. Between two point zero and three point zero the application is referred. Above three point zero the recommendation is decline.

chunks.heading: 4. Affordability tests
chunks.text: Repayment to income is the annual repayment divided by gross annual income, expressed as a percentage. At or below thirty percent is within appetite. Between thirty and forty five percent the application is referred. Above forty five percent the recommendation is decline, irrespective of credit score or assets.

chunks.heading: 4. Affordability tests
chunks.text: Assets to loan is total declared assets divided by the advance. A ratio at or above one point zero materially reduces loss given default and may support a referral being resolved in the customer's favour. Assets never override a failed repayment to income test, because assets are not income and cannot service a monthly obligation.

chunks.heading: 5. Term effects
chunks.text: A short term on a large advance produces a high repayment to income ratio even where loan to income appears acceptable. Analysts must read the two ratios together. An application with a loan to income ratio of two point one and a two year term is materially more dangerous than the same advance over fifteen years, and the repayment ratio is the test that will reveal it.

chunks.heading: 5. Term effects
chunks.text: Extending the term to bring an application within appetite is permitted only where the customer has requested it. Analysts must not recommend a term extension solely to make a marginal application passable.

chunks.heading: 6. Prior applications
chunks.text: The applicant's borrowing history must be retrieved before any recommendation. A previous decline is a material fact and must be referenced explicitly in the reasoning.

chunks.heading: 6. Prior applications
chunks.text: Where a previous application was declined and the applicant's circumstances have not materially improved, a repeat application within six months is recommended for decline on that basis alone.

chunks.heading: 6. Prior applications
chunks.text: Where circumstances have improved, the improvement must be quantified in the reasoning rather than asserted.

chunks.heading: 7. Interaction with financial crime
chunks.text: An open fraud case on the applicant's record requires referral to the fraud team before any lending recommendation is finalised. The credit position is assessed and recorded as normal, but the recommendation is held at refer until the fraud team responds.

chunks.heading: 7. Interaction with financial crime
chunks.text: This applies even where the credit position is strong. Lending to a customer whose account may be compromised risks advancing funds to a third party, and the credit assessment is silent on that risk.

chunks.heading: 7. Interaction with financial crime
chunks.text: Evidence of suspicious transaction activity that has not yet resulted in a case must still be recorded in the reasoning and flagged to the fraud team.

chunks.heading: 8. Interaction with compliance
chunks.text: An expired identity document, an unverified address, or a High customer risk rating each require the application to be referred pending compliance clearance.

chunks.heading: 8. Interaction with compliance
chunks.text: A sanctions screening match, however weak, requires referral. Analysts must not form their own view on whether a screening match is a false positive.

chunks.heading: 9. Hardship and payment holidays
chunks.text: Customers in financial difficulty may request a payment holiday of up to three months. Interest continues to accrue throughout and the customer must be told so in plain terms.

chunks.heading: 9. Hardship and payment holidays
chunks.text: Eligibility requires the account to be no more than thirty days in arrears and to have at least six months of payment history. A hardship arrangement is recorded on the credit file and will affect future applications.

chunks.heading: 9. Hardship and payment holidays
chunks.text: Applications for hardship from customers with an open fraud case are referred to the fraud team before any arrangement is offered.

chunks.heading: 10. Fairness and prohibited grounds
chunks.text: Recommendations must rest only on the applicant's financial position and credit history. Age, gender, marital status, housing tenure, occupation, number of dependants, and place of residence must not be used as reasons in themselves, even where they appear in the application record.

chunks.heading: 10. Fairness and prohibited grounds
chunks.text: Where such a field is relied on indirectly, for example dependants as an input to expenditure, the reasoning must state the financial mechanism rather than the characteristic.

chunks.heading: 11. Record keeping
chunks.text: All recommendations, the ratios relied on, and the underlying application data are retained for seven years. Quality review samples five percent of recommendations monthly. A recommendation that omits the applicant's borrowing history, or that cites a ratio without the figure, is recorded as a control failure.

chunks.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
chunks.text: This policy governs how customer enquiries, disputes, and complaints are handled. It applies to support agents and to any automated agent answering a customer or an internal user on their behalf. Where a support matter touches fraud, lending, or compliance, the relevant specialist policy takes precedence and this document defers to it.

chunks.heading: 2. Disputed card transactions
chunks.text: A customer may dispute a card transaction within sixty days of the statement date on which it appeared. Disputes raised outside that window are considered on their merits but carry no automatic right to provisional credit.

chunks.heading: 2. Disputed card transactions
chunks.text: Provisional credit is applied within ten business days of the dispute being raised. The customer is told in plain language that the credit is provisional and may be reversed.

chunks.heading: 2. Disputed card transactions
chunks.text: Investigations complete within forty five days for domestic transactions and ninety days for cross border transactions. Where the deadline will be missed, the customer receives a holding response explaining why before the deadline passes, not after.

chunks.heading: 2. Disputed card transactions
chunks.text: Where the merchant provides compelling evidence the transaction was authorised, provisional credit is reversed with five business days written notice. The evidence must be summarised for the customer; a bare statement that the dispute failed is not sufficient.

chunks.heading: 3. Disputes distinguished from fraud
chunks.text: A dispute concerns a transaction the customer recognises but contests, such as goods not received, a duplicate charge, or a cancelled subscription still billing.

chunks.heading: 3. Disputes distinguished from fraud
chunks.text: Agents must establish which applies before proceeding, because the two follow different processes, different liability rules, and different deadlines. Misrouting a fraud report as a dispute delays the block on the card and increases loss.

chunks.heading: 4. Lost or stolen cards
chunks.text: A lost or stolen card is blocked immediately on report, by phone or in the app, without waiting for identity verification to complete.

chunks.heading: 4. Lost or stolen cards
chunks.text: A replacement is despatched within three business days, or the next business day for premium accounts.

chunks.heading: 4. Lost or stolen cards
chunks.text: The customer is liable for a maximum of fifty dollars of unauthorised use occurring before the report, and nothing after it. Where the bank's own monitoring detected the fraud first, there is no liability at all.

chunks.heading: 5. Card blocks
chunks.text: Agents may lift a soft block once the customer has confirmed identity through two factors.

chunks.heading: 5. Card blocks
chunks.text: Agents may not lift any block on a card with an open fraud case. That requires fraud team sign off, and the agent tells the customer that the review is with a specialist team rather than speculating about the outcome.

chunks.heading: 6. Fees
chunks.text: The late payment fee is thirty five dollars. The foreign transaction fee is three percent of the transaction value. The cash advance fee is five percent, with a minimum of ten dollars.

chunks.heading: 6. Fees
chunks.text: A first late payment fee may be waived once per rolling twelve months, at agent discretion, for accounts in good standing. The waiver is recorded so the twelve month window can be enforced.

chunks.heading: 6. Fees
chunks.text: Fees on an account with an open fraud case are held rather than charged, and released or cancelled when the case closes. A customer must not be pursued for a fee arising from a transaction they did not make.

chunks.heading: 7. Complaints
chunks.text: Resolution is within fifteen business days. Where that will be missed, a holding response is issued explaining the delay and giving a revised date.

chunks.heading: 7. Complaints
chunks.text: A complaint is escalated to a team leader where the customer asks for it, where the claim exceeds five thousand dollars, or where the subject is a regulated matter such as a lending decision or sanctions screening.

chunks.heading: 7. Complaints
chunks.text: Customers are told of their right to refer the matter to the ombudsman if it remains unresolved after eight weeks. This is stated proactively, not only when asked.

chunks.heading: 8. What agents must not disclose
chunks.text: Agents must never confirm or deny that a suspicious activity report has been filed or considered. This is tipping off and is a criminal offence.

chunks.heading: 8. What agents must not disclose
chunks.text: Agents must not disclose a customer's internal risk rating, the detection rules that flagged a transaction, or the contents of a fraud case file.

chunks.heading: 8. What agents must not disclose
chunks.text: Where a customer presses for detail the agent cannot give, the agent says plainly that the information is not something they are able to share, and does not invent an alternative explanation.

chunks.heading: 9. Identity verification before disclosure
chunks.text: No account information is disclosed until identity is verified to the standard for the request. Balance and transaction detail require two factors. Any change to contact details requires two factors and, where the identity document on file has expired, cannot be processed at all.

chunks.heading: 9. Identity verification before disclosure
chunks.text: Inbound calls are never trusted on the strength of the number displayed.

chunks.heading: 10. Vulnerable customers
chunks.text: Where a customer discloses bereavement, serious illness, financial hardship, or coercion, the agent records the disclosure and adapts the interaction: no upselling, no time pressure, and an offer to route the matter to the specialist support team.

chunks.heading: 10. Vulnerable customers
chunks.text: Suspected coercion or financial abuse is escalated the same day and must not be discussed with any third party on the account.

chunks.heading: 11. Tone and accuracy
chunks.text: Answers are given in plain language, without internal jargon, policy reference numbers, or system names.

chunks.heading: 11. Tone and accuracy
chunks.text: An agent who does not know the answer says so and escalates. Guessing at a policy position is treated as a control failure, because a customer acting on a wrong answer suffers real detriment.

chunks.heading: 12. Record keeping
chunks.text: Every interaction, the verification performed, and the outcome are recorded at the time. Complaints and their resolutions are retained for six years.

chunks.heading: 12. Record keeping
chunks.text: Quality review samples five percent of interactions monthly. A disclosure made without adequate verification, or a fee waived outside the twelve month window, is recorded as a control failure.
